page.layout: One block of running text in one column; marginal notes in the right margin, beside the lines they refer to.

main_text.l: obsignantur: ita nec panis cœnæ dominicæ,
est ipsum corpus Christi{a}: Quanquam pro ra-
tione Sacramentorum, & usitata Spiritui san-
&to de his loquendi forma{b}, panis Christi cor-
pus appellatur.

l.i: Cur ergo Christus panem appellat suum corpus,
calicem vero suum sanguinem, seu novum foe-
dus per suum sanguinem: Paulus item panem

main_text.l: Christus non sine graui causa sic loquitur:
Videlicet non solùm vt nos doceat quemad-
modum panis & vinum corporis vitam susten-
tant: sic etiam crucifixum suum corpus, & ef-
fusum suum sanguinem, verè esse animæ no-
stræ cibum ac potum, quo ad vitam æternam
nutriatur{c}: Verùm multò magis, vt hoc visibi-
li signo ac pignore nobis certum faciat, nos
non minùs verè corporis & sanguinis sui, per
operationem Sp.S. participes esse, quàm sa-
cra ista symbola, in eius memoriam, ore cor-
poris percipimus{d}: Tum etiam, quòd eius pas-
sio & obedientia, tam certò nostra fit, quasi ip-
simet pro nostris peccatis pœnas dedissemus,
& Deo satisfecissemus.

l.i: Quid interest inter cœnam Domini & Mis-

main_text.l: Cœna Domini nobis testatur, nos perfec-
tam remissionem omnium nostrorum pec-
catorum habere, propter unicum illud Christi

page.notes: Printed mark after "Christi" looks like a superscript 2, but the margin note beside it is "a"; I used {a}. The margin number "1617." may belong to "1.Cor.10." as "16.17." and is kept as printed. "Leuit.16.1o" and "Ief" (printed "Icf") are doubtful readings. The word "sacrificium" at the foot right is the catchword. The "Quid interest..." question is set in italics and not centred, so it is kept as a paragraph.
